issues.desc: Scope/factual tension on the canonical doc: CHK-001 context says "Update the central policy wording" and lists story-lifecycle.md as the first relatedDoc, but the one-round/typo/wording-only language is NOT in story-lifecycle.md. It lives only in done-closure-runbook-assistant-execution-plan.md:353 ("typo-only") and scope-check-missing-guidance-execution-plan.md:251 ("wording-only"). story-lifecycle.md:190 instead states audit-round escalation is "threshold-triggered, not documentation-triggered" (>=2 round-1 reviewer findings), which is a DIFFERENT framing than the category-based one-round/three-round rule the checklist assumes. PLAN must pin down exactly which docs carry the editable language and reconcile the category framing with story-lifecycle.md threshold framing, or an implementer could add a contradictory clause to story-lifecycle.md.

"annotation compliance" may be a NEW classification, not just wording consistency. Today the docs only carve out typo-only / wording-only changes to specific documents; neither names annotation compliance. Adding it to the low-risk one-round bucket may be a substantive policy broadening, which conflicts with the story self-framing ("docs-only, do not broaden the low-risk bucket"). PLAN should either cite where annotation compliance is already treated as one-round, or acknowledge this is a new classification needing decision rigor rather than a wording fix.

riskSignal Compliance/Privacy is a likely keyword false positive (mention-vs-modify, B-30b2): "compliance" matched on "annotation compliance" (a Lattice review concept), not GDPR/PII. This elevated priority to high and keeps the 2-item story off the fast channel + triggers high-risk PLAN gates (decision + >=3 preMortem) for a docs-only chore. If truly unrelated to real compliance/privacy semantics, main agent should dismiss via lattice story_review_dismiss category=Compliance/Privacy; dismissing it (with 0 remaining riskSignals) reverts priority and enables the fast channel.

CHK-002 is a non-regression guard, not an independent deliverable: it largely restates the negative of CHK-001 (verify the three-round path was not broken) rather than a distinct unit of observable work. Acceptable, but the two items are not cleanly orthogonal.

verificationIntent references "lattice convergence_check --json" but convergence_check --help reports "No arguments"; confirm the global --json flag is accepted, and clarify how convergence_check (requirements/tests convergence) actually evidences "annotation compliance" specifically. PLAN-refinable.
